title: Valorization of Canadian food processing residues for renewable natural gas production  via  anaerobic digestion
content: The incorporation of three main Canadian food processing residue (FPR) streams in anaerobic digestion (AD) operations is evaluated, focusing particularly on their potential for renewable natural gas (RNG) generation. Nationwide production rates of potato and beet, cattle slaughterhouse, and dairy processing wastes are estimated to determine their suitability for biofuel production. A region-specific forecast conducted for Alberta (Canada) suggests a local abundance of untapped agro-industrial residues of up to 337 300 wet tons in 2026 and 434 400 wet tons in 2035. These substrate candidates were further found to offer logistical advantages for their use in anaerobic digestion. Wet, mesophilic biochemical methane potential (BMP) experiments additionally revealed that size-homogenized potato peel residues (PPR) and spent beet pulp (SBP) achieved significantly greater methane potentials than their untreated counterparts. Pseudo-first-order and modified Gompertz modelling supported improvements of 43.4% for PPR and 109.1% for SBP respectively, values which were 24.0% and 91.8% greater than the CH4 potential observed for cattle manure. Exploratory Spearman analysis complementarily indicated that no individual substrate physicochemical property was strongly associated with BMP, yet stronger associations were observed with total biogas yield and apparent kinetic behavior. Furthermore, using environmental and economic benchmarking, potato and beet processing residues are identified as promising candidates for future co-digestion optimization with cattle manure to supplement RNG production in Canada.
